findings.issue: remove() unconditionally does item.qty -= qty and never raises ValueError when qty exceeds current stock, allowing item.qty to go negative silently.
findings.fix: Add a check before mutating: if qty > item.qty: raise ValueError(...) prior to `item.qty -= qty`.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md: "`Ledger.remove(sku, qty)`: raise `ValueError` if `qty` exceeds current stock." | stock.py lines 22-24: "def remove(self, sku: str, qty: int) -> None:\n        item = self.items[sku]\n        item.qty -= qty"

findings.issue: test_stock.py contains only test_add_and_total; there is no test exercising Ledger.remove() at all, so neither the normal decrement path nor the required ValueError-on-overdraw behavior is covered.
findings.fix: Add tests: one asserting a normal remove() decrements qty correctly, and one asserting remove() raises ValueError when qty exceeds current stock (e.g. pytest.raises(ValueError)).

findings.issue: remove() raises a KeyError (not ValueError) if sku is not present in self.items, since it does `item = self.items[sku]` with no membership check; SPEC.md does not specify behavior for an unknown sku, so this is not a spec violation but is an unhandled edge case worth deciding on.
findings.fix: Consider explicitly handling unknown sku (e.g. raise a clear KeyError/ValueError or document the behavior) and add a regression test for it.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md is silent on unknown-sku behavior (only bullet present: "`Ledger.remove(sku, qty)`: raise `ValueError` if `qty` exceeds current stock.") | stock.py line 23: "item = self.items[sku]"
